_note: All movement and body numbers live here so the game can be tuned without touching code. Speeds are in mountain time.
_slopes: Slopes are from a 31 m elevation grid, which smooths real faces: a 45 degree cell hides much steeper steps.
_limits: Fixed ropes are the only aid. Walk below climb_start_deg; scramble (slow, tiring) up to no_rope_max_deg; above that only on a fixed rope. Unroped, ground steeper than the surface's stand_deg makes you slide. Clipped in, you can climb anything near the rope.
_rope: Clipped in, you move freely up to rope_leash_m from the rope. Moving along it gets the jumar speed; the rope steers you gently back toward its line and catches slips.
_altitude_pace: Speed multiplier for an acclimatized climber without bottled oxygen.
_slips: Chance per mountain minute of slipping when scrambling unroped at the no-rope limit, rising from climb_start_deg, scaled by pushing and the surface. Standing still is safer but not safe.
_surfaces: slide_drag: how much a sliding body ploughs and loses speed, per m/s per second (deep and wet snow most, ice least). speed: walking/climbing pace multiplier. stand_deg: steeper than this unroped and you slide. friction: sliding friction (you slide on anything steeper than atan(friction)). arrest: extra friction from self-arresting. slip: how slippery it is to scramble on. impact: how much a hard hit on it hurts.
_momentum: You speed up and slow down over momentum_s real seconds instead of instantly, and turning sharply costs speed. Running downhill (Shift) on ground steeper than trip_start_deg can trip you head-first; walking down carefully rarely does.
_steps: On scrambling ground and steeper each step is a separate placement. The slip chance is per step: careless steps (pushing, or turning sharply mid-step) are riskier, and holds on loose rock can crumble.
_rockfall: Off for now (rockfall_enabled). Loose rock knocked off by the climber, and natural rockfall from steep rock faces above, most in the warm afternoon. Rocks bounce down the terrain in real time and hurt if they hit you.
_snow_types: Above crust_above_m the wind packs open snow slopes into a hard, slippery crust. Afternoon sun softens snow below soften_below_m into slush: warmth peaks at sun_peak_hour and lasts sun_soft_hours either side.
_breath_pace: Up high you take several breaths for every step uphill. Pushing the pace means skipping push_breath_skip of them, which builds a breath debt; let it pass gasp_debt and you stop to gasp until it clears. It pays back slowly at a steady pace and quickly standing still.
_descent: Most accidents happen on the way down: downhill steps slip more often.
_snow: You sink into snow by the surface's sink_m, less where it is already trodden. Sinking slows you and costs effort; your own footprints pack the snow, so the way back is easier.
_rope_falls: Slipping while clipped in drops you until the rope comes tight (your distance from the rope plus rope_slack_m), with a pendulum if you were off to the side. The jolt hurts above rope_safe_jolt_m_s.
_rope_failure: Fixed ropes are old and anchored in snow, ice and rock of mixed quality. Each time the rope comes tight on a fall there is a rope_fail_chance that the anchor rips out or the rope breaks, plus rope_fail_per_m_s for every m/s of the jolt. Then you fall free, unroped.
_orientation: How you are sliding decides how well you can self-arrest: on your front feet-first is best. Holding Space rolls you onto your front (roll_over_s) and swings your feet downhill (swing_round_s).
_ledges: The 31 m elevation grid smooths away the small ledges, steps and snow terraces of a real face. ledge_share of the ledge_cell_m cells on steep ground hold one (ledge_radius_m across): ground there counts ledge_relief_deg flatter, so you can stand on it, and a slide over it gets ledge_friction more grip.
_falls: Falls run in real seconds. A fall starts as a slide: hold Space to self-arrest, which only works below self_arrest_below_m_s, and works again whenever a runaway slide slows back down. You tumble only when you leave the ground for tumble_airborne_s, hit hard, or go over ground steeper than tumble_slope_deg; on gentler ground a tumble settles back into a slide after tumble_settle_s. Tumbling loses energy fast (tumble_friction and tumble_drag). Air drag uses the body's drag area and mass and thins with altitude. Damage comes from how hard you hit the ground (speed into it above safe_impact, squared, times impact_damage and the surface's impact) and from scraping over rock at speed, never from distance alone.
_tumble_drag: Every bounce and scrape of a tumbling body costs energy, roughly in proportion to speed squared (per metre per second, per second). With friction this keeps a tumble down a 45-55° face around 15-25 m/s, as the coarse terrain has none of the real face's bumps.
_self_arrest: Bare-handed self-arrest (digging in hands, elbows and boots) only works below self_arrest_below_m_s and adds the surface's arrest grip. An ice axe will raise both later: see Climber._arrestTool().
_ice_axe: With the axe in hand (I draws or stows it; drawing it takes axe_draw_s) self-arrest works up to axe_arrest_below_m_s with axe_grip times the surface's grip, building up over axe_bite_s as the pick bites. On ice the pick skates (axe_ice_grip). Over axe_rip_above_m_s the axe can be wrenched from your hands; in a tumble you lose your grip often. It hangs on its leash until you regrab it (axe_regrab_s), and the leash can snap (axe_leash_snap) and the axe is gone: restock one at a camp (G). Climbing, the axe lets you go up snow and ice to axe_climb_max_deg unroped, stand (with crampons) on snow and ice up to axe_stand_deg and slip less, but slower and harder.
_axe_wall: Snow and ice steeper than axe_climb_max_deg (up to axe_wall_max_deg) can only be climbed swing by swing: each click plants the axe and pulls you axe_swing_m up the slope over axe_swing_s, costing axe_swing_stamina. Between swings you hang on the axe and your grip drains (axe_grip_drain_per_s at 45°, faster when steeper or tired); at 0 you come off. Grip recovers on easier ground, on a ledge or clipped in. A placement can skate off (axe_skate_chance, more on ice).
_survival: The climber's body over hours and days, in mountain time. See src/sim/physiology.js. Weather and terrain can override the air (climber.environment) and add effects (climber.effects).
_camp_stores: What each camp has to resupply from with G. -1 means as much as you like. Oxygen is stocked high on the mountain, as Sherpa teams do.
_gear: Gear packed at Base Camp (src/sim/gear.js). Shelters can't go on ground steeper than shelter_max_deg unless on a ledge. Without crampons, every slip chance on snow and ice is multiplied by no_crampons_slip.
_o2_altitude_drop: How many metres lower the air feels at each flow in litres per minute.
_sleep: Press Z by a camp tent (within tent_reach_m of it) to sleep. From night_from_hour you sleep until wake_hour the next morning; in the day it is a nap of nap_hours. full_rest_hours or more fully restores stamina; each hour asleep heals sleep_health_per_hour, but never permanent injuries.
_crevasses: Glacier crevasses come in fields of parallel cracks across the flow, at most one field per crevasse_cell_m cell: crevasse_share of glacier cells (more where the ice steepens) hold one, cracks crevasse_spacing_m apart, bowed up to crevasse_bow_m. Open slots gape crevasse_open_width_m (half-width, at the middle of a field) with ragged edges. Up to two deep pits or moulins (pit_share each, pit_radius_m) sit above and below a field down the flow; snowfield_crevasse_share on the high snowfields between snowfield_crevasse_m. Below bare_glacier_below_m the glacier is bare and most are open; above it hidden_share_snow are hidden under snow bridges. serac_tower_share of the steepest glacier cells hold an ice tower instead.
_bridges: Each step on a hidden snow bridge can break it: bridge_collapse_per_step times (1.2 - its strength), times bridge_warm_mult in the warm afternoon (bridge_cold_mult in the frozen night and early morning; cross glaciers early). Pushing the pace stamps harder. A slide over one breaks it slide_bridge_break of the time. Probing (X) finds hidden crevasses within probe_reach_m in front of you and takes probe_seconds of mountain time.
_holes: Falling into a crevasse: the walls narrow and slow you (hole_wall_drag per second) until you wedge on the snow plug at its depth; the landing hurts like any hard hit, softened by hole_landing_impact. Climbing out is slow and exhausting without ice tools: hole_climb_m_per_h at sea level, scaled for altitude, with hole_climb_slip_per_min chances of peeling off back to the bottom.
_cornices: Off for now (cornices_enabled): the lips looked like stray white lines from a distance. Stepping out onto a cornice can break it: cornice_break_per_step times how far out you are (0 at the crest, 1 at the lip) squared, times overhang_mult for snow overhangs, more in the warm afternoon. A section is cornice_section_points crest points (about 6 m each) long; cornice_top_m is how far the snow stands above the crest.
_seracs: Serac icefall comes off a hanging serac serac_fall_per_hour times per mountain hour on average (more in the afternoon), as ice blocks that bounce down the fall line. It is separate from rockfall (rockfall_enabled), which stays off.
_serac_blocks: Whether the hanging seracs are solid ice cliffs (drawn as one cliff each). Glacier ice towers are off for now (serac_tower_share 0): they looked out of place.
_path_lights: Lamp posts every path_light_every_m along the glacier trail from Base Camp, and a little closer up the rope to Camp 1. Groups further than path_light_draw_m from you aren't drawn.
_caverns: Resting in a snow cave or ice cavern heals at cavern_health_regen_per_hour, out of the wind.
